# T112 — `check` reports the state of the policy repo

**Branch:** work on this branch (`feat/policy-repo-check`); it already carries this brief.
**Size:** M · **Rules:** [README](README.md) · **Needs:** T108, T111 (#98), both on `main`.
**Runs alongside:** T110 on `feat/policy-repo-hook`. You share no file; do not edit theirs.
**Design:** [2026-11-25-policy-repo-design.md](../superpowers/specs/2026-11-25-policy-repo-design.md),
section 5. Where this brief and the design differ, the brief wins.

## Goal
`check` tells a person when their clone of the policy repo is missing, points at the wrong repo,
is at a different commit from the one their knowledge was built against, or has policy files that
changed since; and it reports broken, ambiguous or duplicated entries in the repo's index.
`check` stays read-only.

## Facts
- `checkTree(dir)` in `scripts/lib/check.mjs` (line ~218) validates state, then adds issues
  `{ rule, severity, file, line?, message, hint }`. The company branch (line ~322) already holds
  the `standards/index-missing` and `standards/index-no-trigger` rules; follow their shape.
- `scripts/lib/policyrepo.mjs` gives `policyRepoProblem`, `policyRepoStatus` (read-only git probes,
  status `ok | missing | not-a-clone | wrong-remote | moved | no-git`, plus `head`),
  `readPolicyIndex` (entries, topics, `problems: [{ line, reason }]` with reasons
  `missing-target`, `leaves-clone`, `absolute`, `url`, `backslash`, `symlink`, `not-a-file`,
  `not-markdown`, `unreadable`, `empty-target`, `ambiguous-topic`) and `usablePolicyRepo`.
- T111 records, per project, `policy: { commit, files: { '<repo path>': sha256 } }` in
  `.devocd/refresh.json`. Company `policyRepo.builtAt` is **not** written by anything.
- `check.mjs` must not import `knowledge.mjs` or `refresh.mjs`: both import `check.mjs`. Find the
  pages that cite a topic with `parsePageMeta` from `scripts/lib/pagemeta.mjs` over the project's
  `code/` and `flows/` pages.
- `findRepeats(layers)` in `scripts/lib/redundancy.mjs` finds repeated sentences and bullets
  across layers.

## Decided by the controller
1. **Where each rule runs.** Company check: `missing`, `wrong-remote`, `no-git`, the index rules
   and `duplicate`. Project check (a project whose company records a repo): `version` and
   `changed`, against that project's `refresh.json`.
2. **`version` compares the clone's HEAD with the project's recorded `policy.commit`,** not with
   company `builtAt`. No recorded `policy` (an older baseline) gives no issue.
3. **`changed` reports, it does not mark.** `check` writes nothing. It warns once per changed or
   deleted linked file and names the pages that cite its topic; `refresh-status` already lists
   them as stale.
4. **`policy/unused` is not in this task.** It needs the per-pointer record T110 adds to
   hook-stats; it becomes T112b after both merge.
5. **No git status probe outside `policyRepoStatus`.** No fetch, no network.

## Rules

| Rule | Severity | Where | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| `policy-repo/missing` | error | company | status `missing` or `not-a-clone` |
| `policy-repo/wrong-remote` | error | company | status `wrong-remote` |
| `policy-repo/no-git` | info | company | status `no-git` (git-based rules skipped) |
| `policy-repo/version` | warning | project | clone HEAD ≠ the project's `policy.commit` |
| `policy-repo/changed` | warning | project | a linked file's sha256 differs from the recorded one, or it is gone |
| `policy/missing-target` | error | company | an index line with reason `missing-target` (file = the index, with its line) |
| `policy/bad-link` | warning | company | any other refusal reason except `ambiguous-topic` |
| `policy/ambiguous-topic` | warning | company | reason `ambiguous-topic` |
| `policy/duplicate` | warning | company | `findRepeats` over the linked repo files finds a repeated rule |

Messages name repo-relative paths and short commits (7 characters), never file contents.
Hints say what to do (`git pull`, then `/devocd:refresh`; fix the index line; and so on).

## Also in this task
`trace` run on the company folder itself reports a repo policy as `{ external }` without path and
commit, because `policyCloneOf` in `scripts/lib/trace.mjs` uses `findScope(...).company`, which is
null for a company. Make it use the scope's own state when it is a company. One test.

## Owns
- `scripts/lib/check.mjs`: the new rules, in one function called from `checkTree`
- `scripts/lib/policyrepo.mjs`: new exports only if a rule needs a helper (do not change existing
  ones)
- `scripts/lib/trace.mjs`: `policyCloneOf` only
- Tests: new tests in `check.test.mjs` (one table for the rules), `policyrepo.test.mjs`,
  `trace.test.mjs`
- `docs/TASKS.md`: the T112 line. `docs/briefs/QUEUE.md`: the T112 row.

**Do not touch:** `scripts/devocd-hooks.mjs`, `parent.mjs`, `integrations.mjs`, `hookstats.mjs`,
skills (T110's), `knowledge.mjs`, `refresh.mjs`. Need another file → `NEEDS_CONTEXT`.

## Tests
- One table, one row per rule, over real `gitRepo` fixtures (a second commit for `version`, an
  edited linked file for `changed`, a changed `origin` for `wrong-remote`, a removed folder for
  `missing`). Each row asserts rule, severity and file; one row asserts nothing is written
  (state, `refresh.json` and the clone unchanged, `git status --porcelain` empty).
- A company without `policyRepo` gets none of these rules.
- Show each new test fails without its code.

## Done when
- `npm test`, `npm run coverage` (98% gate, `scripts/lib` not lower), `npm run mutants` and
  `node scripts/validate-plugin.mjs` pass locally; numbers in the PR.
- The PR lists every git argv the check path runs (expected: only T108's probes).
- PR to `main` with the status line, Interpretations, Validation and Limits.
